inspection_summary: Inspected all 740 normalized lines. The source sets a lower-mean-value problem for analytically continued generalized Dirichlet series, separates Euler-product and no-Euler-product routes, and develops reusable mechanisms based on contour transfer, subharmonic control, zero detection and interval pruning, Dirichlet-polynomial mean values, finite differences, truncated inverses, and second/fourth-moment interpolation. All three v1 units remain source-supported, but each needs bounded surrounding context; two exact claims remain unsafe because their formulas are damaged in the normalized extraction.

sections_inspected.label: Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the generalized mean-value problem, states the Euler-product versus no-Euler-product program, records sample lower bounds, and identifies the upper-bound obstruction.

sections_inspected.label: Euler-product hypotheses and main statements
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Specifies two Euler-product coefficient regimes, states Theorems 1 and 2, and transfers a maximal shifted-line bound to the critical line by a contour argument.

sections_inspected.label: Initial contradiction bounds and local analytic control
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Turns failure of the desired lower bound into an upper bound, derives subharmonic pointwise control from a local area mean, and bounds local zero counts with Jensen's inequality.

sections_inspected.label: Zero detection, good intervals, and the asymptotic lemma
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds a density estimate using a truncated reciprocal, removes zero-near intervals, approximates the function by a Dirichlet polynomial, and extracts its coefficient-square main term.

sections_inspected.label: Coefficient growth, finite differences, and completion of the Euler-product case
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Connects coefficient-square growth to mean-value lower bounds, converts separated values to derivatives by finite differences, handles the alternative Euler-product condition, and records a relaxed coefficient-growth variant.

sections_inspected.label: No-Euler-product argument
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States Theorem 3, substitutes a truncated series and truncated inverse for Euler-product zero detection, discards bad intervals, and uses a bilinear Dirichlet-series mean-value lemma for a lower bound.

sections_inspected.label: Balasubramanian's moment remark
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Sketches a route from a second-moment asymptotic and fourth-moment upper bound to a first-moment lower bound.

accepted_units.title: Good-interval approximation and coefficient-square main-term extraction
accepted_units.why_material: On intervals separated from zeros, represents the powered series by a smoothed Dirichlet polynomial plus a controlled contour error, replaces restricted integrals by full-interval moments, and identifies the diagonal coefficient-square series as the main term.

accepted_units.title: Finite differences as averaged derivatives
accepted_units.why_material: Expresses an alternating finite difference of function values as an iterated average of the m-th derivative, providing the bridge from value mean bounds to derivative mean bounds.
accepted_units.context_note: The identity is stated for an m-times continuously differentiable function and positive step size; proof is deferred to induction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate formula dependence; binomial typography is noisy but the finite-difference/iterated-integral identity is recoverable.

accepted_units.why_material: Chooses a chain of nearby real parts, combines coefficient-derived lower bounds with dominance between shifted means, and applies the finite-difference lemma to show that some derivative mean must be large.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the completion under condition (ii); exact constants and exponents in the display should be checked from the scan.

accepted_units.title: Condition (i) completed by comparing value differences with the first derivative

within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A contradiction upper bound enables zero-density control and deletion of zero-near intervals; on the remaining intervals a Dirichlet-polynomial diagonal term exposes coefficient growth, and finite differences transfer value lower bounds to derivative lower bounds.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Structural comparison of Euler-product and no-product routes
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The Euler-product route obtains coefficient growth after zero detection and good-interval approximation, whereas the no-product route compensates by multiplying truncated series and reciprocal approximants, excluding large-error intervals, and extracting a diagonal term through a bilinear mean-value estimate.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The no-product result is explicitly restricted to 2k=1 here and has weaker bounds; the source does not establish equivalence of the two mechanisms.
